title: Ivo and the Room
premise: Bram Brightwater has spent seven years as night nurse at Marlowe House, a hospice where the dying count backwards from ten and the walls breathe when no one watches. When the village's church bell—melted down in 1911—rings at midnight, the residents begin signing a mysterious ledger that appeared in the parlor, and Bram realizes the house is collecting its final verse. The bell tolls the 'Room Song,' a hymn whose last verse has never been sung; whoever completes it opens the Room behind the linen closet, and whoever hears it whole belongs to the house forever. To save the last resident, nine-year-old Ivo, a ward no family claimed, Bram must learn the final verse without ever singing it aloud—discovering along the way that the house's hunger is grief itself, and that the Room only wants what no one else would keep. In the end, Bram sings the last verse alone, offering themself in Ivo's place, and the house—recognizing at last a love freely given rather than duty performed—releases them both, its bell falling silent as the found family walks out into morning.
about_author: Mirabel Hartwell is the pen name of a former hospice volunteer who spent three years in a converted Victorian sanatorium and never quite stopped listening for the bell. They write horror about the tenderness that survives in haunted places, and live with two cats who refuse to enter the spare room.

chapters.title: The Counting
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. On a routine night shift, dying resident Mrs. Aldous counts backwards from ten and stops at four, whispering 'the bell knows the rest.' Bram rationalizes it, as they always have, but the linen closet door stands open for the first time in seven years. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of routine cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: A Bell That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At midnight the church bell rings—though parish records confirm it was melted down in 1911. The village hears nothing; only the hospice residents stir, some smiling in their sleep. Bram finds a ledger on the parlor table with nine signatures already written in a hand like their own. Emotional beat: denial curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Ivo
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The nine-year-old ward, unclaimed by any family, reveals he's heard the bell his whole life and knows it's 'looking for its last singer.' He shows Bram the Room behind the linen closet—doorframe only, warm air breathing out. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other, the seed of found family.

chapters.title: The Verse Before Last
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Digging through the sanatorium's 1911 archives, Bram learns the bell was cast with a hymn—the Room Song—and that the foundress sang all but the final verse the night she vanished. The residents begin humming in unison at night. Emotional beat: the past pressing its hand flat against the present.

chapters.title: Signatures
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Residents sign the ledger one by one, each growing lighter, more translucent, humming fragments of the song. Bram tears out pages; they reappear whole. Ivo begs Bram not to let him sign. Emotional beat: love against duty—Bram's job is to ease passing, but now passing itself is the trap.

chapters.title: What the House Keeps
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Room opens a crack; inside, Bram glimpses everyone the house has ever 'kept,' including the foundress, still waiting mid-verse. The house speaks through the dying: it is not cruel, only unbearably lonely, and it believes a finished song means a finished family. Emotional beat: horror reframed as grief, sympathy for the monster.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, flashback-laced. Bram confronts why they chose invisibility—the family that erased them, the identity they buried to survive—and realizes the house has been mirroring their own self-erasure all along. Ivo refuses to let Bram disappear the way Bram disappeared themself. Emotional beat: identity confronted; the theme turns inward.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Everyone else has signed; only Ivo remains, and the house begins singing the last verse through the walls, pulling him toward the linen closet in his sleep. Bram wakes to find Ivo's hand already holding the pen. Emotional beat: desperation, the clock running out, love refusing to let go.

chapters.title: The Final Verse
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the midnight toll, Bram steps between Ivo and the Room and sings the last verse alone—voice breaking, meaning every word as an offering. The house hesitates; the foundress finally finishes her own verse through Bram's mouth; the Room exhales and goes dark. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice freely given, the one thing duty could never be.

chapters.title: Morning Bell
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The bell falls silent forever; the ledger crumbles to ash; the residents who signed pass gently, unafraid, their names remembered. Bram, changed but whole, adopts Ivo, and they leave Marlowe House together as the sun rises over a village that never heard a thing. Emotional beat: resolution—found family, love outlasting the house, the quiet after the song.
